findings.description: The configuration's timeout setting and what it means to apply it are undefined. RM0486 sections 59.7.2–59.7.3, pages 2989–2990, describe separate prescaler and reload values, so a verifier cannot determine the required peripheral configuration from the stated input.
findings.requested_change: Define the timeout input and its required relationship to the peripheral settings, including any necessary units or controlled reference.

findings.description: The requirement promises a counter reload on every refresh invocation. RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2984, states that a refresh request can be ignored while a previous refresh is still in progress.
findings.requested_change: Specify the conditions and driver response for refresh requests so the promised outcome is achievable under the documented hardware behavior.

findings.description: The rejected window-value range depends on an undefined configuration representation. RM0486 section 59.7.5, page 2992, describes a register field but does not define the caller's value or its conversion. OP-DRV-002 defers the range, leaving the acceptance boundary unverifiable.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-DRV-002 as blocking

findings.description: The trigger refers to a valid comparison value without defining validity. RM0486 section 59.7.6, pages 2992–2993, specifies a field width and a lower constraint, but the requirement does not define the caller's representation or acceptance criteria.
findings.requested_change: Define or precisely reference the valid input domain for the early-wakeup configuration service.

findings.description: The cited RM0486 section 59.4.2, page 2981, identifies IWDG internal signals; it does not establish the reset-cause flag or its meaning. OP-DRV-005 acknowledges that the flag's source has not been identified.
findings.requested_change: Identify and cite the document section and page that define the reset-cause flag and verify that the service matches its semantics.

findings.description: The accepted range of the timeout setting cannot be determined without knowing its representation and mapping to prescaler and reload values. RM0486 sections 59.7.2–59.7.3, pages 2989–2990, describe hardware fields, while OP-DRV-002 defers the range decision.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-DRV-002 as blocking

findings.description: Leaving the window setting unchanged when the option is off does not establish whether window operation is disabled: a previously configured window may remain active. RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2982, describes the default window value and its effect, not an independent option switch.
findings.requested_change: Clarify the intended behavior when the caller disables or omits the option, including the case of an existing non-default window setting.

findings.description: The requirement combines writing the prescaler selection and writing the reload value. Either setting can be applied correctly while the other is wrong, so the two outcomes can pass or fail independently.
findings.requested_change: Separate the prescaler and reload obligations into independently verifiable requirements.

findings.description: The requirement identifies the supplied comparison value as the counter position for the interrupt. RM0486 section 59.6, page 2986, and section 59.7.6, page 2993, instead relate the interrupt to a counter value one less than the programmed comparison value.
findings.requested_change: Define the caller value and its relationship to the programmed comparison value and interrupt position consistently with the cited sections.

findings.description: The requirement says the prescaler selection is written unchanged, but does not define whether the caller supplies a divider or its register encoding. RM0486 section 59.7.2, pages 2989–2990, distinguishes the encoded field from the resulting divider, so the two interpretations require different writes.
findings.requested_change: Define the caller-facing representation of the prescaler selection and its relationship to the peripheral setting.

findings.description: The requirement associates the interrupt with one counter position. RM0486 section 59.7.6, page 2993, describes a comparison that also includes lower counter values and conditions interrupt generation on the enable bit. The single-position description does not capture that behavior.
findings.requested_change: State the source-supported comparison and enable conditions without implying that only one counter position can satisfy the interrupt condition.

findings.description: The comparison condition says it covers the supplied value minus one and lower counter values, but does not exclude higher counter values. RM0486 section 59.7.6, page 2993, specifies an upper boundary for the comparison.
findings.requested_change: State the complete comparison boundary so that a verifier can determine whether counter values above it must be excluded.

findings.description: The requirement unconditionally requires application of a valid value, but RM0486 section 59.7.4, page 2991, restricts updates while EWU is set, and DRV-IWDG-021 requires a timeout if a pending update does not complete within the wait limit. In that case the driver cannot guarantee application.
findings.requested_change: Qualify the application obligation for the pending-update timeout case and specify the observable outcome consistently with DRV-IWDG-021.

findings.description: The caller-facing window value representation and accepted range are undefined. RM0486 section 59.7.5, page 2992, describes a hardware field but does not define the caller's representation. The rejection boundary cannot be verified.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-DRV-002 as blocking and define the caller-facing representation and acceptance boundary.

findings.description: The accepted timeout-setting range is not specified for the caller-facing prescaler selection and reload value. RM0486 sections 59.7.2–59.7.3, pages 2989–2990, describe hardware fields; OP-DRV-002 leaves the acceptance boundary unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-DRV-002 as blocking and define the accepted range of each caller-facing timeout field.

findings.description: The comparison condition includes the supplied value minus one and lower counter values but does not exclude higher values. RM0486 section 59.7.6, page 2993, specifies an upper boundary.
findings.requested_change: State the complete comparison boundary, including the exclusion of counter values above it.

findings.description: The requirement unconditionally requires application of a valid value, but RM0486 section 59.7.4, page 2991, restricts updates while EWU is set, and DRV-IWDG-021 requires a timeout if a pending update does not complete within the wait limit.
findings.requested_change: Make application conditional on the update being permitted and reconcile the timeout outcome with the early-wakeup configuration requirements.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-009 and DRV-IWDG-024 specify valid early-wakeup values, but the set does not state the response to an out-of-range value or whether it may change hardware. DRV-IWDG-014 names an invalid-argument status without defining this trigger.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-006 requires issuing a refresh request, while DRV-IWDG-022 requires success when the counter has actually reloaded. findings.description: DRV-IWDG-001, 007, 023, 024 and 029 require configuration writes or effects for valid requests without accounting for pending updates. findings.description: CON-IWDG-007 requires an already-running status when start is called while the watchdog is running. This requirement limits that response to a valid configuration, while invalid-argument requirements apply to invalid configurations without excluding the already-running case.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the status precedence for an already-running watchdog and an invalid configuration in accordance with CON-IWDG-007.

findings.description: The requirement demands an already-running status even for a null or invalid configuration. DRV-IWDG-002, DRV-IWDG-008, DRV-IWDG-017 and DRV-IWDG-038 require an invalid-argument status for their respective invalid inputs without excluding an already-running watchdog. The requirements therefore prescribe conflicting results for the same calls.
findings.requested_change: Make the invalid-argument requirements and already-running status precedence consistent in their normative statements.

findings.description: The rationale says invalid configurations receive the status specified by the validation requirements, but DRV-IWDG-043 says an already-running status takes precedence for those configurations.
findings.requested_change: Align the rationale with the resolved status precedence.

findings.description: The explicit reload is conditioned on an automatic reload taking effect, but the rationale says the window write may leave the value unchanged and does not rely on it to load the counter. RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2982 and 2985, describes a reload on a value change and a reload after an update; the requirement does not define the outcome if the assumed automatic reload does not occur.
findings.requested_change: Specify a bounded, verifiable sequence and outcome that also covers an unchanged window value, consistent with CON-IWDG-009.

findings.description: The requirement makes the reload request conditional on an unspecified settling delay. OP-DRV-014 defers its numeric value, leaving a verifier unable to determine when the request must be issued or whether the preceding automatic reload has completed. RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2985, relates completion to a prescaler clock edge.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-DRV-014 as blocking

findings.description: CON-IWDG-007 requires an already-running status whenever start is called on a running watchdog, without an exception for an invalid configuration. DRV-IWDG-043 limits that status to valid configurations, while OP-DRV-015 treats the precedence as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Align the already-running and invalid-argument requirements with CON-IWDG-007 for calls on a running watchdog, and resolve OP-DRV-015 accordingly.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-043 requires an already-running status even for an invalid configuration, while DRV-IWDG-002, DRV-IWDG-008, DRV-IWDG-017 and DRV-IWDG-038 require an invalid-argument status for applicable invalid inputs without excluding a running watchdog. DRV-IWDG-014 makes those statuses distinct, so both obligations cannot be met for the same call.
findings.requested_change: Align the invalid-argument requirements with the already-running precedence required by CON-IWDG-007, so each start call has one consistent status.

findings.description: The rationale says invalid configurations receive the validation requirements' status, while DRV-IWDG-043 gives already-running status precedence.
findings.requested_change: Align the rationale with the resolved status precedence and the corrected validation requirements.

findings.description: The reload request depends on an unspecified settling delay. OP-DRV-014 defers its value, so the request timing and completion of a preceding automatic reload cannot be verified. RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2985, relates that completion to a prescaler clock edge.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-DRV-014 as blocking.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-043 requires already-running status for invalid configurations, while DRV-IWDG-002, 008, 017 and 038 require invalid-argument status without excluding a running watchdog. DRV-IWDG-014 makes the statuses distinct.
findings.requested_change: Apply the specified precedence consistently to the affected validation requirements.

findings.description: RM0486 sections 59.4.4 and 59.6, pages 2982–2987, describe configuration-induced reloads and their timing. The set does not establish the caller-visible interaction with a subsequent refresh. DRV-IWDG-037's rationale also describes a window reset threshold differently from section 59.4.4.
findings.requested_change: Correct the threshold rationale and resolve or explicitly block the caller-facing timing and refresh interaction.

findings.description: Success is conditional on the counter having been loaded, but DRV-IWDG-035 and 040 require only issuing reload requests. RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2984, says a request can be ignored while a previous refresh remains incomplete; no completion observation is specified.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile the success condition with observable hardware behavior and CON-IWDG-008, or identify and resolve the decision needed to specify a verifiable outcome.

findings.description: The requirement makes two successive different window writes and waits only for the first window update. RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2985, places the automatic reload after the update flag clears; page 2984 describes ignored refreshes while a previous refresh is incomplete. The set does not establish that the second write's reload completes.
findings.requested_change: Establish a source-supported bounded sequence or other verifiable means to ensure the requested counter load, including the interaction between the two writes.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-009 sets the accepted timeout range to 1–1000 ms, but the service response to a value outside that range is left to OP-DRV-013. This caller-visible invalid-input behavior is needed at the requirements boundary.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-DRV-013 as blocking.

findings.description: The set does not define the caller-visible effects of configuration-induced reloads on the timing of later refreshes. OP-DRV-011 defers whether to report or guard the interaction, although the decision can change the driver interface and permitted caller behavior.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the caller-visible contract at this stage, or classify the unresolved decision as blocking.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-040 adds a settling delay after the bounded window-update wait, but the set does not say whether that delay is included in the caller's timeout. CON-IWDG-004 and 009 require hardware waits to be bounded and to report timeout when unfinished.
findings.requested_change: Define how the settling delay is bounded and how it relates to the service's caller-supplied timeout.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-001, 002 and 006, UC-IWDG-001, 003 and 008, and RM0486 sections 59.2, 59.4.4, 59.7, 59.7.1, 59.7.3 and 59.7.5 are partially covered because start success, successive configuration reloads, and subsequent refresh timing remain unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the identified start and reload interactions and update the affected interface requirements and traceability.

findings.requested_change: classify OP-DRV-014 as blocking

findings.description: RM0486 sections 59.4.4 and 59.6, pages 2982–2987, describe configuration-induced reloads. Their effect on subsequent caller refresh timing remains unresolved in OP-DRV-017.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-017 and specify the resulting caller-visible interaction.

findings.description: Success now depends on a load having been requested, but the start sequence does not establish that the load takes effect. RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2984–2985, describes refresh overlap and delayed automatic reload; OP-DRV-016 leaves the window-enabled sequence unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-016 and specify a verifiable start outcome consistent with the chosen sequence.

findings.description: Two different window writes are separated by the first update's completion, but RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2984–2985, places automatic reload after that update and describes ignored overlapping refreshes. The set does not establish the second reload's completion.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-016 and specify a sequence whose required counter load can be verified.

findings.requested_change: classify OP-DRV-013 as blocking

findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-017 and specify the affected service behavior and caller obligations.

findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-016 and OP-DRV-017 and complete the affected requirements.

findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-016 and OP-DRV-017 and complete the affected requirements and traces.

findings.description: The accepted range includes 4095 when the window option is enabled, but RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2982, identifies that value as disabling the window option. The requirement therefore accepts a configuration that cannot produce the selected behavior.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the enabled-window range so that accepted values enable window operation, and align the associated interface requirements.

findings.description: The requirement rejects every encoding above 7, excluding the distinct divide-by-1024 setting supported by RM0486 section 59.7.2, page 2990. The rationale's one-to-one encoding argument does not justify removing that divider from the driver interface.
findings.requested_change: Provide an input-supported reason for excluding the divider, or define an accepted encoding for it.

findings.description: The requirement associates the request with loading the counter, but an early-wakeup configuration write can trigger an earlier reload and RM0486 sections 59.4.4 and 59.6, pages 2984 and 2986, describe reloads that may not yet be complete when another request is issued. Clearing update flags alone does not establish that the requested load takes effect.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the start sequence and its stated outcome against the documented reload timing, or record the missing product decision as a blocking open point.

findings.description: RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2982–2985, describes both a configuration-induced reload and a reset condition for a reload above the window. Waiting for update flags alone does not establish that the additional request loads the counter safely. OP-DRV-019 leaves this unresolved, so the requirement's stated outcome cannot yet be assured.
findings.requested_change: classify OP-DRV-019 as blocking

findings.description: The requirement prescribes behavior for a separate early-wakeup configuration service, while CON-IWDG-010 restricts that configuration to the start service. OP-DRV-018 records that the intended interface is undecided.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-018 and align the requirement with the chosen configuration interface.

findings.description: For a start call on a running watchdog with an invalid wait limit, this requirement requires invalid-argument status, while DRV-IWDG-043 requires already-running status regardless of configuration validity. The precedence asserted in the rationale is absent from the requirement text; CON-IWDG-007 and CON-IWDG-012 also state competing outcomes.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the precedence between the product decisions and state the resulting behavior consistently in the affected requirements.

findings.description: The timeout response combines returning a timeout status with issuing no counter reload request. Either behavior can fail independently of the other.
findings.requested_change: Separate the status response and the prohibition on a reload request into independently verifiable obligations.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-012 requires an invalid-parameter status without hardware access for every out-of-range timeout, while CON-IWDG-007 requires an already-running status for every start call on a running watchdog. The requirement selects one outcome for their overlapping case, but the inputs do not establish that precedence.
findings.requested_change: Record a blocking open point for the conflicting outcomes and resolve the precedence with the product owner before specifying the result.

findings.description: The condition applies when the start-service wait limit is reached, but the prohibition on issuing a counter reload request has no stated duration or service boundary. It can be read as prohibiting later refresh-service requests as well as the start-service request described in the rationale.
findings.requested_change: Define the period and service to which the prohibition applies.

findings.description: The clause requiring the driver to issue a reload request 'without making any statement' about the counter does not identify an observable driver behavior or a defined interface statement. It is unclear what would satisfy or violate that part of the requirement.
findings.requested_change: State the observable reload-request obligation and place the qualification about unconfirmed completion in the rationale or a defined interface requirement.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-035 requires a reload request once all update flags are clear but does not exclude flags clearing after the wait limit. DRV-IWDG-048 prohibits a reload request from that point until the start call returns, so the requirements conflict if the flags clear during that interval.
findings.requested_change: Define the reload obligation for flags clearing within the permitted wait and align its timeout behavior with DRV-IWDG-048.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-012 requires an out-of-range timeout to be rejected without hardware access. DRV-IWDG-045 prohibits access only to the watchdog peripheral, allowing access to other hardware.
findings.requested_change: Align the hardware-access prohibition with CON-IWDG-012 for the cases covered by this requirement.

findings.description: Returning an invalid-argument status and avoiding hardware access are independently testable obligations: either can hold while the other fails.
findings.requested_change: Separate the status and hardware-access obligations so each can be judged independently.

findings.description: The condition that all update flags clear before the wait limit does not require the reload request itself to occur after they clear. A request issued earlier in the same call could satisfy the stated obligation, contrary to CON-IWDG-010 and the configuration sequence in RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2984.
findings.requested_change: Require the reload request to occur only after all register-update flags are clear.

findings.description: The requirement excludes a start call on a running watchdog, but CON-IWDG-012 requires no hardware access for every out-of-range wait limit. OP-DRV-021 concerns the conflicting return statuses and does not resolve or contradict that access prohibition.
findings.requested_change: Apply the no-hardware-access obligation to every call with an out-of-range wait limit, including a start call on a running watchdog.

findings.description: The requirement demands a reload request before the wait limit whenever all update flags become clear before that limit. The flags could clear just before the limit, leaving less time than the driver needs to observe them and issue the request. CON-IWDG-009 specifies a 1 ms tick but gives no response-time margin that makes this obligation feasible.
findings.requested_change: Define the deadline behavior using an observable flag check and allow for the time needed to issue the request, while preserving the timeout behavior required by CON-IWDG-009 and CON-IWDG-010.

findings.description: A flag check can find every flag clear immediately before the wait limit, leaving insufficient time to issue the required reload request before that limit. OP-DRV-022 acknowledges that no response-time margin is specified, so tying the obligation to the check alone does not make the deadline feasible.
findings.requested_change: Define a feasible condition for issuing the request that accounts for the time remaining after the check, and specify the outcome when the request cannot be issued before the limit.

findings.description: The requirement mandates a reload before the limit whenever a check finds all flags clear before the limit, but also permits the limit to be reached before that request. It then invokes DRV-IWDG-044, which requires a timeout only if the limit is reached before all flags are clear. Thus the stated fallback does not cover the case where the flags were already clear.
findings.requested_change: Make the reload and deadline conditions consistent, and specify an applicable outcome for a limit reached after the successful flag check but before the request.

findings.description: The requirement promises that the explicit request loads the counter, but RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2982–2985, describes both reset on an early refresh and ignored requests while a previous refresh is incomplete. Clear update flags alone do not establish the stated outcome.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-DRV-019 as blocking and resolve the safe window-enabled start sequence and its observable outcome.

findings.description: The requirement specifies a separate early-wakeup configuration service, while CON-IWDG-010 confines that configuration to the start service. OP-DRV-018 records the unresolved interface conflict.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-018 and align the early-wakeup requirements and service boundary with the decision.

findings.description: A check can find all flags clear immediately before the wait limit, leaving no established margin to issue the mandatory request before that limit. OP-DRV-022 defers the missing response-time decision, but feasibility of the obligation depends on it.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-DRV-022 as blocking.

findings.description: The requirement both mandates a request before the limit after a successful flag check and permits the limit to arrive first. Its fallback invokes DRV-IWDG-044 and DRV-IWDG-048, whose conditions require the limit to arrive before all flags are clear, so they do not cover that case.
findings.requested_change: Make the request and timeout conditions consistent and specify the outcome when flags were clear but the request was not issued before the limit.

findings.description: The rationale assigns invalid configurations the validation requirements' status, while DRV-IWDG-043 requires already-running status for a start call on a running watchdog.
findings.requested_change: Correct the rationale to match the applicable status requirements and the unresolved overlap in OP-DRV-021.

findings.description: Success follows a load request even when the request may overlap a configuration-induced reload. RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2984–2985, describes ignored overlapping refreshes; OP-DRV-020 leaves the acceptance criterion unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-020 and state a verifiable success criterion consistent with the selected start sequence.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-007 requires already-running status for start on a running watchdog, while CON-IWDG-012 requires invalid-parameter status for an out-of-range wait limit. DRV-IWDG-043 selects already-running for the overlap, although OP-DRV-021 records that precedence as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-021 and align the status requirements with the decision.

findings.description: Unlike DRV-IWDG-035, the window-enabled load requirement does not bound the request by the caller's wait limit or specify the outcome when that limit is reached before the request. It also does not explicitly order application of the window value before the request.
findings.requested_change: Specify the window-enabled start ordering and the bounded-wait and timeout outcomes consistently with CON-IWDG-009 and CON-IWDG-010.

findings.requested_change: Resolve the permitted window configuration and start sequence, then specify a sequence that does not cause an unintended reset.

findings.description: The separate early-wakeup configuration service conflicts with CON-IWDG-010, which confines configuration to the start service.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the early-wakeup interface and make the requirements consistent with the decision.

findings.description: The rationale attributes the status for invalid configurations to validation requirements, while DRV-IWDG-043 specifies already-running status for a start call on a running watchdog.
findings.requested_change: Correct the rationale to describe the status precedence actually specified, subject to OP-DRV-021.

findings.description: Success follows a load request even when a preceding configuration-induced reload may still be in progress. RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2984–2985, describes requests that can be ignored during a preceding reload; OP-DRV-020 leaves the acceptance criterion unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve whether issuing the request suffices for success or whether its effect must be confirmed, and specify the selected acceptance criterion.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-007 requires already-running status for start on a running watchdog, while CON-IWDG-012 requires invalid-parameter status for an out-of-range wait limit. DRV-IWDG-043 selects already-running for their overlap although OP-DRV-021 records precedence as undecided.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the status precedence and align the affected requirements with the decision.

findings.description: UC-IWDG-004 and CON-IWDG-010 are partially covered: the requirements specify a separate early-wakeup configuration service while the product decision confines configuration to start.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the interface decision and cover early-wakeup configuration consistently in the selected interface.

findings.description: RM0486 section 59.4 and UC-IWDG-003 are partially covered because the required window-enabled start request has the safety issue identified for DRV-IWDG-036.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the window configuration and sequence, then establish coverage of the window-enabled start.

findings.description: RM0486 section 59.7 coverage is partial because the unresolved window-enabled start and early-wakeup interface affect its register sections.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-023 and OP-DRV-018 and align requirements for the affected register capabilities.

findings.description: UC-IWDG-001 and the start-up scenario are partial: DRV-IWDG-016 specifies success after a request whose acceptance may be unresolved, and DRV-IWDG-036 specifies a potentially unsafe window-enabled request.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-020 and OP-DRV-023 and align start behavior and success criteria.

findings.description: UC-IWDG-007, CON-IWDG-012 and invalid-input coverage are partial: the returned status for a start call with an out-of-range wait limit while the watchdog is running conflicts with the unresolved precedence in OP-DRV-021.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-021 and specify the applicable status consistently.

findings.description: The obligation applies when the early-wakeup value is valid, even if another argument, such as the wait limit, is invalid. In that case CON-IWDG-012 and DRV-IWDG-049 prohibit hardware access during the call, so the value cannot be applied.
findings.requested_change: Condition application on all start-service arguments being valid and on the service continuing past validation.

findings.description: The obligation applies when the early-wakeup value is valid, even if the caller supplies an invalid wait limit. CON-IWDG-012 and DRV-IWDG-049 prohibit hardware access during that call, so the interrupt cannot be enabled.
findings.requested_change: Condition interrupt enablement on all start-service arguments being valid and on the service continuing past validation.

findings.description: The success trigger is satisfied once settings are applied, the watchdog is started and all update flags are found clear before the limit. If the limit then expires before the reload request, DRV-IWDG-044 requires timeout for the same call, while this item still requires success.
findings.requested_change: Define the success condition to exclude the timeout path, including expiry between the flag check and the required reload request.

findings.description: RM0486 section 59.7.2, page 2990 maps encoded values 8 through 15 to the same divider. The requirement rejects 9 through 15 solely to enforce a one-to-one encoding, but the cited inputs do not establish that driver acceptance policy as a product decision.
findings.requested_change: Obtain an authorized decision for the restricted encoding domain or revise the accepted domain to avoid the unsupported restriction.

findings.description: The second timeout condition refers to the reload request of DRV-IWDG-035 without limiting the condition to configurations where that request is required. With the window option enabled, DRV-IWDG-035 does not require the request, leaving the condition applicable after the flags clear and potentially until the call returns.
findings.requested_change: Limit the second timeout condition to the non-window case and define the window-enabled completion boundary consistently with DRV-IWDG-016.

findings.description: The flag check is required after the watchdog starts, but the item does not require the check to follow application of all start configuration settings. A check made before a later configuration write could satisfy the stated ordering even though CON-IWDG-010 requires the start service to wait for the register updates before the first load request.
findings.requested_change: Order the qualifying flag check after the relevant configuration writes and before the reload request.

findings.description: The requirement obliges the driver to apply the comparison value once a pending update completes, without excluding a call whose wait limit expires first. DRV-IWDG-032 instead requires the setting to remain unwritten when that limit is reached.
findings.requested_change: Condition application on the pending update completing before the wait limit, and make the timeout path consistent with DRV-IWDG-032.

findings.description: The requirement obliges the driver to enable the interrupt once a pending early-wakeup update completes, without excluding a call whose wait limit expires first. DRV-IWDG-032 requires the setting to remain unwritten when that limit is reached.
findings.requested_change: Condition enabling on the pending update completing before the wait limit, and make the timeout path consistent with DRV-IWDG-032.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-015 requires the start service to write the settings and then wait for all update flags to clear before returning success. This requirement does not order its flag check after the configuration writes; for the window-enabled case, an earlier clear check can therefore satisfy the stated success condition while a later update remains pending.
findings.requested_change: Require the qualifying check that finds all update flags clear to occur after the final configuration write.

findings.description: The requirement combines applying the comparison value when the pending update completes in time with leaving the value unapplied when the wait limit is reached first. Either behavior can pass while the other fails; the timeout behavior is also specified in DRV-IWDG-032.
findings.requested_change: Keep the successful application obligation in this item and reference the separate timeout obligation without restating it as an additional obligation.

findings.description: The requirement combines enabling the interrupt when the pending update completes in time with not enabling it when the wait limit is reached first. These outcomes can pass or fail independently; DRV-IWDG-034 separately addresses the timeout path.
findings.requested_change: Keep the interrupt-enable obligation in this item and reference the separate timeout obligation without restating it as an additional obligation.

findings.description: Returning success and refraining from confirming a counter reload are independently judgeable behaviors. A start service could return the required status while still attempting confirmation, or omit confirmation while returning the wrong status.
findings.requested_change: Specify the success status and the prohibition on reload confirmation as separate obligations.

findings.description: The obligation applies when the early-wakeup update is clear before the wait limit, even if a different required update remains pending until that limit. DRV-IWDG-021 then requires the service to return timeout, but this item still requires the early-wakeup value to be applied.
findings.requested_change: Condition application on the start service reaching the early-wakeup configuration step without an earlier timeout, consistent with the timeout path.

findings.description: The early-wakeup update can be clear before the wait limit while another required update remains pending until that limit. In that case this item requires the interrupt to be enabled, but DRV-IWDG-034 prohibits enabling it after the timeout.
findings.requested_change: Condition enabling on the start service reaching that step without an earlier timeout, consistent with DRV-IWDG-034.

findings.description: The requirement permits the enable step whenever no earlier timeout occurred, including while an early-wakeup register update is still pending. RM0486 section 59.7.6, page 2992, requires the EWU flag to be clear before the interrupt-enable bit can be changed. DRV-IWDG-031 defers writes to settings but does not explicitly cover the separate interrupt-enable operation.
findings.requested_change: Require the pending early-wakeup update to complete before enabling the interrupt, and align the timeout path with the existing bounded-wait requirements.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-015 requires the start service to issue no extra load request after writing the window value. DRV-IWDG-035 instead requires a load request after every configuration setting has been written when the window option is disabled. DRV-IWDG-023 requires the service to configure the window setting in that case, including when a previously applied setting must be changed.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the disabled-window start sequence against CON-IWDG-015 and make DRV-IWDG-023 and DRV-IWDG-035 consistent with the resulting decision.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-001 and DRV-IWDG-029 require configuration writes when the structure is valid and the watchdog is stopped, without conditioning those writes on a valid wait limit or completion of earlier waits. DRV-IWDG-049 prohibits hardware access for an invalid wait limit, and DRV-IWDG-032 and DRV-IWDG-034 restrict writes and later steps after a timeout.
findings.requested_change: Make the start-service write obligations conditional on successful validation of all arguments and on the relevant waits completing before the timeout.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-015 requires the start service to write the early-wakeup setting. DRV-IWDG-009 and DRV-IWDG-024 address only configurations that enable the option; the set does not specify what start does to the early-wakeup setting when the option is disabled.
findings.requested_change: Specify the required early-wakeup configuration for the disabled option, including its treatment of any previously applied setting, or record a blocking open point if the inputs do not determine it.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-015 starts the watchdog after the timeout settings are applied, whereas RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2983–2984, presents configuration sequences that start it before the configuration writes. The set does not establish that its reversed sequence produces the intended initial counter load: RM0486 section 59.4.3, page 2981, describes the counter starting from its reset value.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the start and configuration sequence against the hardware behavior and CON-IWDG-015, and specify the resulting initial counter behavior or raise a blocking open point for any necessary product decision.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-001 and DRV-IWDG-029 now require valid arguments and completion of their respective pending updates, but do not condition their writes on completion of earlier waits. If an earlier wait times out, DRV-IWDG-021 returns a timeout and DRV-IWDG-034 prohibits dependent later steps, while a later write can still be required by DRV-IWDG-001 or DRV-IWDG-029.
findings.requested_change: Condition each configuration write on reaching that step without an earlier timeout, and make the timeout exit and subsequent-step obligations consistent across the start sequence.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-015 requires start to write the early-wakeup setting. DRV-IWDG-051 requires the interrupt to be left disabled when the option is off, but does not require the early-wakeup setting to be written or specify the comparison value in that case.
findings.requested_change: Specify the disabled-option early-wakeup write and its value if supported by the product decision, or record the missing decision as a blocking open point.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-015 starts the watchdog after the timeout settings are applied. RM0486 section 59.4.3, page 2981, describes start from the counter reset value, while section 59.4.4, pages 2983–2984, presents start before configuration. The initial counter behaviour and compatibility with the product's no-extra-load decision remain unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-030 and make the start sequence and initial counter behaviour consistent with the selected product decision and the hardware.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-007 and DRV-IWDG-023 require window configuration when the watchdog is stopped without requiring a valid wait limit or successful completion of earlier steps. An invalid wait limit prohibits all hardware access under DRV-IWDG-049; an earlier timeout can require the start service to return under DRV-IWDG-021.
findings.requested_change: Condition both window paths on successful argument validation and reaching the window step without an earlier timeout.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-015 requires starting with a valid configuration structure but does not require a valid wait limit or completion of earlier waits. DRV-IWDG-049 prohibits hardware access for an invalid wait limit, and DRV-IWDG-034 prohibits starting after a timeout of a prerequisite setting.
findings.requested_change: Condition starting on all arguments being valid and all prerequisite steps having completed without timeout, in addition to resolving OP-DRV-030.

findings.description: Coverage partial: CON-IWDG-002 - Start and configuration gaps are tracked by the findings on DRV-IWDG-007, DRV-IWDG-015 and SET; CON-IWDG-013 replaces the separate early-wakeup configuration service.
findings.requested_change: Cover CON-IWDG-002 with a requirement, or record an open point if the inputs do not say enough.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-015 requires the start service to write the early-wakeup setting. DRV-IWDG-051 leaves the interrupt disabled when the option is off but does not specify whether or how its comparison value is written. OP-DRV-031 records the unresolved product decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-031 and specify the option-off early-wakeup setting consistently with the resulting product decision.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-015 starts the watchdog after applying the timeout setting. RM0486 section 59.4.3, page 2981, identifies the initial counter value, while section 59.4.4, pages 2983–2984, presents start before configuration. The resulting initial counter behavior and its relationship to CON-IWDG-015 remain unresolved in OP-DRV-030.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-030 and specify a consistent start sequence and initial counter behavior.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-024 requires enabling early wakeup for a valid configuration and stopped watchdog while also saying the enable occurs only if the wait limit was not reached earlier. If an earlier prerequisite times out, DRV-IWDG-021 requires a timeout return and DRV-IWDG-034 prohibits dependent steps, but the trigger of DRV-IWDG-024 still applies.
findings.requested_change: Condition the enable obligation on reaching that step without an earlier timeout and on the applicable wait completing before its limit.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-051 requires the start service to leave early wakeup disabled for valid arguments when its pending update completes, but does not condition this obligation on reaching the step without an earlier timeout. DRV-IWDG-021 requires return on timeout, and DRV-IWDG-034 prohibits dependent later steps.
findings.requested_change: Condition the option-off obligation on reaching its configuration step without an earlier timeout, consistently with the other start-service steps.

findings.description: Coverage partial: CON-IWDG-010 - The early-wakeup enable and option-off steps conflict with timeout handling, as described in the findings on DRV-IWDG-024 and DRV-IWDG-051.
findings.requested_change: Cover CON-IWDG-010 with a requirement, or record an open point if the inputs do not say enough.

findings.description: Coverage partial: UC-IWDG-007 - The findings on DRV-IWDG-024 and DRV-IWDG-051 track conflicts between start steps and timeout handling.
findings.requested_change: Cover UC-IWDG-007 with a requirement, or record an open point if the inputs do not say enough.

findings.description: Coverage partial: fault detection and reaction - The findings on DRV-IWDG-024 and DRV-IWDG-051 track inconsistencies between timeout handling and early-wakeup configuration.
findings.requested_change: Cover fault detection and reaction with a requirement, or record an open point if the inputs do not say enough.

findings.description: The condition permits the reload request after any observation that all update flags are clear, including one made before the final configuration write. CON-IWDG-010 and CON-IWDG-016 require the wait after the settings are written; RM0486 section 59.4.4, page 2984, places the refresh after the register updates.
findings.requested_change: Require the qualifying flag check to occur after the final configuration write before the reload request is issued.

findings.description: The obligation applies when an earlier update has timed out and the service has returned, provided the listed early-wakeup update condition was met. DRV-IWDG-021 requires return on that earlier timeout, but this item does not condition the action on reaching the early-wakeup step without an earlier timeout.
findings.requested_change: Condition the obligation on the service reaching the early-wakeup step without having returned a timeout for an earlier update.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-051 requires the interrupt to be disabled regardless of its previous setting, while this item prohibits writing a comparison value. RM0486 section 59.7.6, page 2992, places the interrupt enable and comparison value in the same register; changing the enable by a register write also writes the comparison field. The requirements do not define how both obligations can be met when the enable was previously set.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the requirements for disabling the interrupt and preserving the comparison value in a way that is implementable with the documented register interface.

findings.description: The stated preconditions require a reload request even if an earlier update times out or the final flag check never finds every flag clear within the wait limit. DRV-IWDG-044 and DRV-IWDG-048 instead require a timeout response and prohibit a subsequent reload request in that case.
findings.requested_change: Condition the reload obligation on the start service reaching the final flag check and finding every update flag clear within the wait limit.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-017 prohibits writing a comparison value when the early-wakeup option is off. The requirement instead permits writing the existing value back, as its rationale explicitly allows, so it does not enforce the product decision.
findings.requested_change: State the no-comparison-value-write obligation required by CON-IWDG-017, and resolve its interaction with disabling the interrupt in the shared register using RM0486 section 59.7.6, pages 2992–2993.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-017 prohibits writing a comparison value when the option is off, but RM0486 section 59.7.6, pages 2992–2993, places the interrupt enable and comparison value in the same register. The requirement permits a register write to disable the interrupt without resolving whether the comparison field may be written, or what value it may carry.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-035 and state the permitted register behavior consistently with the product decision.

findings.description: The requirement combines independently verifiable prohibitions: applying a configuration value, writing the register when the interrupt is already disabled, and writing it to set a comparison value. One can be violated while another is satisfied.
findings.requested_change: Separate the independently judgeable obligations and reconcile them with the decision on OP-DRV-035.

findings.description: The restriction on a register write depends on its stated purpose, which is not an observable pass/fail criterion for the specified test. The text also does not specify what comparison field value is permitted in a write used to disable the interrupt.
findings.requested_change: After resolving OP-DRV-035, specify observable conditions and permitted register-write effects so a test can determine whether the requirement is met.

findings.description: The requirement limits writes by their purpose, but does not specify the permitted comparison-field value in a write that disables the interrupt. RM0486 section 59.7.6, pages 2992–2993, places the enable and comparison fields in the same register. A disabling write that changes the comparison field cannot be judged objectively from the stated criterion.
findings.requested_change: State observable criteria for the comparison field during a disabling write, and reconcile them with CON-IWDG-017 and OP-DRV-035.

findings.description: The requirement restricts the purpose of an early-wakeup register write but does not specify the comparison-field value permitted in a disabling write. RM0486 section 59.7.6, pages 2992–2993, places the enable and comparison fields in the same register, so the written value cannot be assessed against CON-IWDG-017 without the decision recorded in OP-DRV-035.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-035 and specify the permitted comparison-field behavior for a disabling write.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-024 requires the interrupt to be enabled for valid arguments and a stopped watchdog, while restricting the action to cases without an earlier timeout. If an earlier prerequisite times out, DRV-IWDG-021 requires a timeout return and DRV-IWDG-034 prohibits the dependent enable step, but the trigger of DRV-IWDG-024 still applies.
findings.requested_change: Condition the enable obligation on reaching the early-wakeup step without an earlier timeout, consistently with the timeout requirements.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-010 requires all update flags to clear before the first load request. CON-IWDG-016 requires the manual's window-enabled sequence, in which the window write causes an automatic reload before the final flag wait; see RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2982–2983. DRV-IWDG-007 and DRV-IWDG-036 implement that sequence, leaving the relationship to CON-IWDG-010 unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Obtain a product decision reconciling the first-load condition with the window-enabled sequence and reflect it in the requirements.

findings.description: The requirement limits the purpose of an early-wakeup register write but does not define the comparison-field value allowed in that write. RM0486 section 59.7.6, pages 2992–2993, places the enable and comparison fields in the same register. Whether preserving the comparison field satisfies CON-IWDG-017 remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-035 and specify the permitted write behavior consistently with the decision.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-010 requires all update flags to clear before the first load request. CON-IWDG-016 requires the window-enabled sequence in RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2982–2983, where the window write causes an automatic reload before the final flag wait. The relationship between these constraints remains unresolved.
findings.requested_change: Resolve OP-DRV-036 and align the window-enabled sequence and first-load condition with that decision.

findings.description: The trigger requires the start service to reach the enable step without an earlier timeout, but a pending early-wakeup update can remain incomplete until the wait limit is reached during that step. This item then requires enabling after completion, while DRV-IWDG-034 prohibits the dependent step after timeout.
findings.requested_change: Condition the enable obligation on the pending update completing within the applicable wait limit, and retain the timeout behavior when it does not.

findings.description: The item independently restricts the purpose of register writes and requires the comparison field to retain its previous content. A write used to disable the interrupt could satisfy the purpose restriction while changing the comparison field, so the obligations can pass or fail separately.
findings.requested_change: Separate the write restriction and comparison-field preservation into independently verifiable obligations.

findings.description: The prohibition on a write 'for the purpose of setting a comparison value' depends on the implementer's intent. The stated test method cannot distinguish that purpose from an otherwise identical write made to disable the interrupt while preserving the field, as permitted by CON-IWDG-019.
findings.requested_change: State the write restriction in terms of observable register operations and field values so a test can determine whether it is met.

findings.description: The trigger permits the case where no early-wakeup update is pending, but the required action says to enable the interrupt only after “that update” completes. It is unclear what event must precede enabling when there is no such update.
findings.requested_change: Define the enable condition for both an already-clear update flag and a pending update that completes before the wait limit.

findings.description: The comparison value must be read after the last preceding access to the early-wakeup register and before the write. That read is itself an access to the register, so it cannot occur after the last preceding access. The stated condition cannot be satisfied as written.
findings.requested_change: Define an achievable, observable comparison against the register field’s valid current value before the write.

findings.description: The requirement mandates a hardware read to obtain the preserved comparison value, while CON-IWDG-019 requires preservation of the current field content and OP-DRV-034 defers how that content is obtained to software design. The mandatory read imposes an unsupported implementation choice.
findings.requested_change: State the required preservation outcome without prescribing how the current field content is obtained, or provide an explicit source and justification for requiring a read.

findings.description: CON-IWDG-016 requires the configuration sequence in RM0486 section 59.4.4, pages 2983–2984. DRV-IWDG-015 orders start before the setting writes, but the set does not order the prescaler, reload and early-wakeup writes relative to the window write. In the window-enabled sequence, the window write loads the counter, so this ordering affects which reload value is used.
findings.requested_change: Specify the applicable ordering of the configuration writes and counter load for each window option, consistent with CON-IWDG-016 and the cited manual sequence.

findings.description: DRV-IWDG-056 requires the start service to write the early-wakeup setting when it writes a valid configuration. DRV-IWDG-053 forbids an early-wakeup register write when the option is off and the interrupt is already disabled. Both conditions can apply to the same start call.
findings.requested_change: Make the sequencing requirement conditional on an early-wakeup write being required, while preserving the order of settings that are written.
